title: Check yourself: Git workflows, committed configuration and versioned prompts

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A developer wants private notes about how they like to work in this repository, visible to nobody else. Which place holds them?

options.text: `.mcp.json`, which lists the servers the whole team uses
options.says: Ruled out because `.mcp.json` holds "The MCP servers a project uses", which is configuration and not notes.

options.text: `.claude/settings.json`, which carries the team's rules to every clone
options.says: Ruled out because the file is committed and holds "Team permission rules, default model, hooks, plugins", so the notes would reach the whole team.

options.text: `CLAUDE.md`, which every session loads before the first prompt is typed
options.says: Ruled out because `CLAUDE.md` is committed and holds "Commands, conventions, the git workflow", which every teammate loads.

options.text: `CLAUDE.local.md`, which stays out of version control
options.says: The table puts "One developer's notes for this project" in `CLAUDE.local.md`, which is "No, in `.gitignore`".

origin.section: What is committed and what is not

questions.stem: A workflow embeds its instruction text in a string, and teammates tweak it whenever an answer looks off. What makes those edits safe to ship?

options.text: A versioned file with a changelog line and a review
options.says: The page says to keep "One file per prompt, in the repository", with "A version in the file", "A changelog entry for every change" and "A review of the change".

options.text: A shorter string of a few lines in the same workflow
options.says: Ruled out because "A reworded prompt is a behaviour change", and a shorter string is still a rewording with no version or review.

options.text: A secret-store entry in place of the repository text
options.says: Ruled out because a prompt in the repository gives a diff and a revert: "a rollback is one revert", which a secret store does not offer.

options.text: A nightly rewrite by Claude from the day's results
options.says: Ruled out because a rewrite nobody reads skips the step the page asks for: "A review of the change, ideally with a sample of inputs whose outputs are compared before and after".

questions.stem: A pull request adds a line to the committed `.claude/settings.json` that allows a new shell command. How should the team treat it?

options.text: As a personal preference, since each developer picks their own rules
options.says: Ruled out because the line "changes what runs on every teammate's machine", so it is shared behaviour and not a private choice.

options.text: As documentation, since the file only describes how Claude should act
options.says: Ruled out because the file holds "Team permission rules, default model, hooks, plugins", which are rules that take effect and not prose.

options.text: As a change to a build script, since it alters what every clone runs
options.says: The page says "a line in `.claude/settings.json` that allows a command or enables a plugin changes what runs on every teammate's machine", so such pull requests "deserve the same care as a change to a build script".

options.text: As a local override, since such lines belong in `.gitignore`
options.says: Ruled out because "a committed file is reviewed like code", and the shared settings file is committed, while the local file is the one kept out of version control.
